_comment: Vanity deployment record. TESTNET ONLY. Testnet token, no value, not officially tradable. Every value is reproducible with scripts/verify-vanity.py; nothing here is hand-transcribed.

create2Deployers.note: First factory. Immutable by design: EIP-684 forbids replacing code on an account that already has it and it exposes no SELFDESTRUCT, so it can never be upgraded. Its limitation is therefore permanent - it cannot forward the ERC-20 supply minted to it as msg.sender, so tokens deployed through it are stranded at this address. See GOL-suffix proof below.

Current factory. Adds deployAndCall(), which forwards the freshly deployed contract's supply to a recipient in the same transaction and leaves no standing authority. Adding the function required a new address, which invalidated every salt mined against the first factory.

deployments.label: GOL-suffix proof (3 bytes)
deployments.name: GOLD
deployments.note: PARTIAL SUFFIX. 474f4c is 'GOL', the first 3 bytes of the full GOLD encoding 474f4c44. NOT the final full-GOLD vanity target.
deployments.finding: Supply is stranded at the factory. CREATE2 makes the factory msg.sender in the constructor, so a standard ERC-20 mints to the factory, which has no ERC-20 interface and cannot transfer. Confirmed live: balanceOf(factory) == 1e26 and a transfer FROM the factory reverts.

deployments.label: GOL-suffix, supply forwarded (3 bytes)
deployments.name: GOLD
deployments.note: PARTIAL SUFFIX, same 3-byte target. Deployed through the factory that has deployAndCall(), so the supply sits with a real EOA and transfers work. This is the deployment used for ERC-20 behaviour checks.
deployments.abandonedNote: First deployment on the current factory. It called transfer(holder, 0) because the amount was left at zero, so the supply stayed at the factory and the deployment was abandoned. Recorded because it is the proof that a CREATE2 salt cannot be reused for a second deployment at the same address.

deployments.label: FULL GOLD vanity target (4 bytes)
deployments.name: GOLD
deployments.note: THE TARGET. Address ends in 474f4c44, the complete ASCII hex encoding of GOLD. Verified three independent ways: the miner's own keccak, Foundry cast keccak, and the factory's on-chain computeAddress().

mining.attemptsNote: salt counter value. With 4 OpenMP threads each scanning a strided band, total attempts is greater than this; the winner simply landed at this counter.
mining.comment: Finished far below the 15-minute mean because the search is geometric: the first match often arrives well before the mean.

deployments.supplyHeldBy: ephemeral test EOA, forwarded by deployAndCall in the deployment tx
deployments.initcodeFrozen: The initcode hash above was re-verified immediately before deployment and was unchanged. Any edit to VanityAsset.sol, the constructor arguments, or the compiler version changes it and kills this salt.
